question: Why would a single fixed endpointing threshold cause problems for a Japanese-speaking user?
options: Japanese audio has a different sample rate
Japanese speakers always speak faster than English speakers
Japanese speakers regularly pause 500ms or more between clauses without yielding their turn, which a short threshold would misinterpret as turn completion
Japanese text requires more tokens to transcribe
explanation: Japanese speakers naturally pause 500ms or more between clauses — much longer than the ~200ms average for English. A fixed threshold calibrated for English would constantly misfire, declaring turn boundaries during normal mid-sentence pauses in Japanese conversation.

question: When should you omit the language hint when configuring the multilingual turn detection model?
options: When you are using Silero VAD
When you want the fastest possible response time
When the user might switch languages mid-conversation and you want the model to adapt dynamically
explanation: For cross-lingual conversations where users might switch languages mid-session, omitting the language hint lets the multilingual model adapt dynamically based on acoustic features rather than being locked to a single language's patterns.
